name: Verified device custody, possession, and remote-control correlation

attribution.legal_posture: Device, shipping, remote-access, and location signals require corroboration and serve as contextual indicators. Mandiant defensive guidance is based on vendor-observed aggregate activity, with Mandiant source-reported aggregate patterns combined with Sophos guidance.

caveats: Alternate shipping addresses, reception desks, relocation services, and equipment depots are common.
Apply controls consistently with privacy, employment, labor, accessibility, retention, notice, correction, and access-governance requirements.
Commercial VPNs, HIDs and alternate shipping addresses all have benign uses and require contextual correlation.
Choose privacy-preserving identity assurance appropriate to law and policy; biometrics and demographic screening require a separate legal and policy basis from this source.
Geolocation is approximate; VPNs, mobile networks, corporate egress, travel, and privacy controls can make it wrong.
Human-interface-device logging and address divergence are contextual controls; DPRK affiliation requires additional source-backed signals.
RMM, KVM, hardware tokens, and activity helpers have legitimate enterprise or accessibility uses; alert on unauthorized combinations rather than product presence alone.
Use the pattern to prioritize documented human-led review; DPRK affiliation, fraud, and malicious intent require a combined evidence record.

statements: Bind approved shipping destination, courier events, asset serial, hardware-backed authentication, enrollment telemetry, and observed device location to the same onboarding case.
Hunt for combinations of unauthorized KVM/RMM, several remote-control products, persistent uptime with little role-expected interaction, and sudden address/location divergence.
Maintain explicit allowlists and exception workflows for IT support, accessibility, travel, relocations, mailrooms, shared workspaces, and managed service providers.
limitations: Geolocation is approximate; VPNs, mobile networks, corporate egress, travel, and privacy controls can make it wrong.
Alternate shipping addresses, reception desks, relocation services, and equipment depots are common.
RMM, KVM, hardware tokens, and activity helpers have legitimate enterprise or accessibility uses; alert on unauthorized combinations, not product presence alone.

statements: Mandiant recommends confirming device delivery and possession during onboarding and reports cases involving multiple remote-management tools, network KVM use, and activity-simulation software after shipment.
limitations: Mandiant-observed patterns and recommendations. Named commercial tools and services have legitimate uses and are not indicators by themselves.

statements: Require in-person pickup of corporate laptops with identity verification when feasible; apply enhanced verification when equipment is shipped somewhere not listed in employment records.
Log human-interface-device connections and monitor new-hire endpoints for remote-access software and VPN use.
Mandiant specifically highlighted Astrill VPN in this 2025 guidance, but use of any commercial VPN is not attribution by itself.

sources.support: The Sophos matrix recommends review of late shipping changes or courier redirection, a defined enhanced-monitoring period for new hires, and correlation of persistent device uptime with limited role-expected activity
